questions.prompt: Complete the third conditional: "If I ___ earlier, I would have caught the train."
questions.explanation: The third conditional requires 'if + past perfect' in the if-clause: 'had left'. "left" uses past simple, which belongs in the second conditional (imaginary present). "have left" uses present perfect, which cannot be used in a third conditional if-clause. "would leave" uses 'would', which belongs only in the result clause.

questions.prompt: Complete the third conditional result: "If she had asked for help, we ___  her."
questions.explanation: In the third conditional, the result clause is 'would/could/might + have + past participle': 'would have helped'. "helped" uses past simple without the modal. "would help" uses 'would + base', which is the second conditional result. "had helped" uses past perfect, which belongs in the if-clause, not the result.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a correct third conditional?

options.text: If he worked harder, he would pass.
If he had worked harder, he would have passed.
If he works harder, he will pass.
If he would work harder, he would pass.

questions.explanation: 'If he had worked harder, he would have passed' is the third conditional: past perfect + would have + past participle. "If he worked harder, he would pass" is the second conditional (imaginary present). "If he works harder, he will pass" is the first conditional (real future). "work" is wrong because 'would' must never go inside the if-clause.

questions.prompt: Complete with the correct result: "If they hadn't missed the meeting, the deal ___."
questions.explanation: The third conditional result can use 'could/might/would + have + past participle': 'might have been closed' correctly uses a passive past participle. "might close" drops 'have' — 'might close' is present/future. "was closed" is a simple past passive with no modal. "would close" uses 'would + base', which is the second conditional.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that expresses a PAST regret using the third conditional.

options.text: If I had had more money, I would have bought a car.
If I have more money, I will buy a car.
If I had more money, I would buy a car.
If I would have money, I would buy a car.

questions.explanation: A past regret uses the third conditional: 'If I had had more money, I would have bought a car.' "If I had more money, I would buy a car" is the second conditional (present/future hypothetical). "will" is the first conditional (real future). "If I would have money, I would buy a car" is wrong because 'would' cannot go in the if-clause.

questions.prompt: Complete: "If the weather ___ better, we could have had the picnic outside."
questions.explanation: The third conditional if-clause uses past perfect: 'had been'. The result 'could have had' confirms this is a past hypothetical. "was" uses past simple — correct for the second conditional (present unreal), not the third. "were" is the formal past simple subjunctive — also second conditional. "would have been" uses 'would have been', which belongs in the result clause, never the if-clause.
